quests.sentence: Scientists demonstrated a clear link between deforestation and accelerated climate change.
quests.hint: 'Demonstrated' is past tense - the finding has already been made and published.
quests.explanation: 'Demonstrated' is the simple past. The sentence describes a completed scientific finding from the past.

quests.sentence: Scientists know that ongoing human activity continues to accelerate global warming.
quests.hint: This describes current scientific understanding - what is known now.
quests.explanation: 'Know' and 'continues' are present tense forms, describing the current state of scientific knowledge.

quests.sentence: Scientists predict that average global temperatures will rise by at least two degrees by 2100.
quests.hint: 'Will rise by 2100' is a future prediction.
quests.explanation: 'Will rise' is the future simple. 'By 2100' is a clear future time reference for a scientific prediction.

quests.sentence: During the financial crisis, house prices fell dramatically across the country.
quests.hint: 'During the financial crisis' is a past historical period.
quests.explanation: 'Fell' is the simple past. 'During the financial crisis' places the event in a completed past period.

quests.sentence: House prices vary considerably depending on location and the level of local demand.
quests.hint: This describes the current, ongoing state of the housing market.
quests.explanation: 'Vary' is the present simple, describing a current, ongoing economic reality.

quests.sentence: House prices will continue to rise in most regions unless significant new housing is built.
quests.hint: 'Will continue to rise' is a future prediction.
quests.explanation: 'Will continue' is the future simple. The sentence makes a prediction about future economic trends.

quests.sentence: Before antibiotics were discovered, many relatively minor infections proved fatal.
quests.hint: 'Before antibiotics were discovered' is a historical past period.
quests.explanation: 'Proved' is the past tense. 'Before antibiotics were discovered' places the statement in a historical past.

quests.sentence: Antibiotics currently save millions of lives every year when they are correctly prescribed.
quests.hint: 'Currently' and 'every year' both signal the present situation.
quests.explanation: 'Save' is the present simple. 'Currently' confirms this describes the present state of medical practice.

quests.sentence: New classes of antibiotics will need to be developed as bacterial resistance grows.
quests.hint: 'Will need to be developed' is a future prediction.
quests.explanation: 'Will need to be developed' is the future simple passive. The sentence predicts a future medical necessity.

quests.sentence: Students once relied entirely on textbooks and face-to-face classroom instruction.
quests.hint: 'Once' signals a past time - things were different then.
quests.explanation: 'Relied' is the simple past. 'Once' places the statement in the historical past.

quests.sentence: Students now learn through a varied blend of digital tools and traditional teaching methods.
quests.hint: 'Now' signals the current educational reality.
quests.explanation: 'Learn' is the present simple. 'Now' confirms this describes the present state of education.

quests.sentence: Artificial intelligence will play an increasingly important role in personalised learning.
quests.hint: 'Will play' is a future prediction about the role of AI.
quests.explanation: 'Will play' is the future simple. The sentence predicts a future development in education.

quests.sentence: Women in most countries were not permitted to vote until the twentieth century.
quests.hint: 'Until the twentieth century' is a historical past period.
quests.explanation: 'Were not permitted' is the past simple passive. 'Until the twentieth century' is a past time reference.

quests.sentence: Equal rights legislation now protects people from discrimination in most countries.
quests.hint: 'Now' signals the current legal situation.
quests.explanation: 'Protects' is the present simple. 'Now' confirms this is the current state of legislation.

quests.sentence: Global campaigns will continue to push for full equality in every country worldwide.
quests.hint: 'Will continue' is a future prediction.
quests.explanation: 'Will continue' is the future simple. The sentence makes a prediction about future activism.

quests.sentence: Early scientists once believed firmly that the atom could not be divided any further.
quests.hint: 'Once believed' places this in a historical past - we now know differently.
quests.explanation: 'Believed' is the past tense. 'Once' signals a historical belief that has since been revised.

quests.sentence: We now know that atoms themselves consist of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
quests.hint: 'Now know' signals current scientific understanding.
quests.explanation: 'Know' is the present simple. 'Now' confirms this is current, established knowledge.

quests.sentence: Future particle physics research will continue to reveal the deeper structure of matter.
quests.hint: 'Future research' hasn't happened yet - it is ahead of us.
quests.explanation: 'Will continue' is the future simple. 'Future research' is a clear indicator that this is a prediction.

quests.sentence: During the Industrial Revolution, millions of people moved from rural areas to cities.
quests.hint: 'During the Industrial Revolution' is a specific historical past period.
quests.explanation: 'Moved' is the simple past. 'During the Industrial Revolution' places the event firmly in the past.

quests.sentence: Urban populations continue to grow as cities offer greater economic opportunity.
quests.hint: 'Continue to grow' describes an ongoing present trend.
quests.explanation: 'Continue' is the present simple. The sentence describes a current, ongoing demographic trend.

quests.sentence: Smart city technology will transform the way urban populations live and work in the future.
quests.hint: 'In the future' and 'will transform' are future markers.
quests.explanation: 'Will transform' is the future simple. 'In the future' confirms this is a prediction about what is to come.

quests.sentence: If the weather was bad during term time, she always caught the bus instead of walking.
quests.hint: The consistent past pattern is described - what she always did when weather was bad.
quests.explanation: 'Was' and 'caught' are past tense forms. This describes a past regular conditional pattern (zero conditional in the past).

quests.sentence: If the weather is bad, she usually takes the bus rather than walking to the office.
quests.hint: 'Usually' signals a general present habit triggered by a condition.
quests.explanation: 'Is' and 'takes' are present tense forms in a zero conditional, describing a current regular pattern.

quests.sentence: If the forecast is bad tomorrow, she will definitely take the bus into town.
quests.hint: 'Tomorrow' is a future time, and 'will take' is the future result.
quests.explanation: 'Will take' is the future simple in a first conditional. 'Tomorrow' confirms this is future.

quests.sentence: If only she had applied for the grant earlier, she would have received the full funding.
quests.hint: 'Would have received' is a past hypothetical result - she didn't apply in time.
quests.explanation: 'Would have received' is the past modal perfect in a third conditional. The earlier application didn't happen.

quests.sentence: If she had more available funding, she would expand the research team immediately.
quests.hint: 'Would expand' is a present hypothetical - she doesn't currently have the funds.
quests.explanation: 'Would expand' is a present conditional. The sentence describes a present hypothetical situation.

quests.sentence: If she secures additional funding next year, she will hire two more researchers.
quests.hint: 'Next year' is a future time, and 'will hire' is the future result.
quests.explanation: 'Will hire' is the future simple in a first conditional. 'Next year' confirms the condition is future.

quests.sentence: The contract was signed by all parties present before the project deadline.
quests.hint: 'Was signed' is the past simple passive - the signing is done.
quests.explanation: 'Was signed' is the past simple passive. The contract has already been signed.

quests.sentence: Contracts are carefully reviewed by the legal team before they are approved for signing.
quests.hint: 'Are reviewed' is the present simple passive for an ongoing process.
quests.explanation: 'Are reviewed' is the present simple passive, describing a current, standard procedure.

quests.sentence: The updated contract will be drafted and circulated by the end of the week.
quests.hint: 'By the end of the week' is a future deadline.
quests.explanation: 'Will be drafted' is the future simple passive. 'By the end of the week' is a future time reference.
